questions.q: In what year did Mahatma Gandhi launch the Non-Cooperation Movement?
questions.a: The movement was launched in 1920. A wrong answer here suggests the student has not yet grasped the timeline of the freedom struggle, requiring a review of the chapter’s historical chronology.

questions.q: Why did Gandhi ask Indians to resign from government jobs?
questions.a: He wanted to withdraw Indian support so the British government could not function. A student who says "to get better jobs" misses the point of non-cooperation as a tool of political pressure rather than personal gain.

questions.q: If you were a student in 1920 supporting this movement, what would you do differently in your daily routine?
questions.a: Steps: 1. Identify the action (boycotting school). 2. Explain the impact (empty classrooms). 3. Connect to the goal (weakening British influence). A wrong answer implies the student thinks the movement was about physical fighting rather than peaceful withdrawal.

questions.q: How does "non-violent resistance" differ from a violent revolt?
questions.a: Non-violent resistance uses refusal to participate, whereas a revolt uses force. Confusing these two shows a failure to understand the philosophy of "satyagraha" as a moral force.

questions.q: Was the Non-Cooperation Movement meant to be a regional protest? Why or why not?
questions.a: No, it was an all-India mass movement involving people across the country. Stating it was regional shows a lack of understanding of the movement's scale and reach.

questions.q: Design a slogan that a person in 1920 might use to explain why they are not paying taxes to the British.
questions.a: The slogan should focus on the idea that "our money should not support those who rule us." A poor answer focuses on greed or laziness rather than the political protest element.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: The Non-Cooperation Movement was a nationwide peaceful protest launched by Mahatma Gandhi in 1920, urging Indians to stop supporting British ______ to weaken colonial rule.

Fill in the blank: Imagine your school authorities pass a rule you feel is unfair, but instead of fighting, you and all your friends simply decide to stop ______ classes, using the library, or following their instructions.
Fill in the blank: The Non-Cooperation Movement was a nationwide peaceful protest launched by Mahatma Gandhi in ______, urging Indians to stop supporting British institutions to weaken colonial rule.
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student must be able to list at least three specific actions of non-cooperation and explain why these actions were considered a challenge to British authority.
